about: Requirements that need a running runtime with an HTTP or WebSocket client. Each case lists the observable check; none can be judged from a fixture run alone.

cases.manual: Against a running runtime: every specified route answers under the prefix; an unauthenticated call is rejected; a bad token is rejected; internal failure returns 5xx not 4xx; a created thread owner equals the caller; POST message returns before a slow execution finishes and the message survives a restart.

Connect the WebSocket: first frame is thread_status; it repeats on every status change; message_data, message_chunk, and event frames appear for their triggers; depth and includeSilent filters drop the right frames; stream_ping gets stream_pong.
With a model that returns reasoning: a connection without the reasoning opt-in receives no reasoning_chunk frames; the reasoning is persisted and returned on message reads and on an opted-in stream.
Delete a parent thread with a running child: new work is refused for both threads, in-flight work is aborted, child streams close, and the delete response arrives only after that.

Create a child whose scoped variables are unset: the create returns a structured bootstrap error with a request id; GET returns the pending requirement; POST stores values and boots the deferred child.
If runtime streams are implemented: open a stream on the execution host, confirm no thread park occurs, and confirm disconnect terminates the stream. Runtimes without streams are conforming.
